newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks slide after news of finance firm woes.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks slide after news of finance firm woes.

text.p: Thai stocks slid 3.69 percent on Monday amid heavy sales after the central bank said 10 finance firms must raise their capital immediately, brokers said.
Finance and bank counters are under suspension and their stocks could not be sold.

"The central bank had said earlier that no Thai finance firms faced liquidity problems. But what they said today contradicted earlier statements," said Thaneit Khantigaroon of Ekachart Finance and Securities.
The index was down 26.85 points to 700.71 at 0809 GNT near the day's low of 700.44.
Three of the 10 finance firms affected were listed and they were International Trust and Finance Plc, Dynamic Eastern Finance Thailand and Sri Dhana Finance and Securities Plc.
Communications, energy and even small capitalised stocks were being sold on the news, brokers said.
The central bank also raised provisions that banks and finance companies needed to make to cover sub-standard assets.
"Investors now believe that they should avoid investing in the stock market because the current situation is not clear," said Thaneit.
